newsitem.title: ALBANIA: Fact-finding IMF mission to arrive in Albania.
newsitem.headline: Fact-finding IMF mission to arrive in Albania.

text.p: A fact-finding mission from the International Monetary Fund (IMF) was due to arrive in Albania on Tuesday for a 10-day stay that will feature talks with leading ministers and officials.

An IMF official told Reuters the mission would meet Finance Minister Alban Malaj, central bank governor Qamil Tusha and also hoped for talks with Prime Minister Bashkim Fino and President Sali Berisha.
"It is mostly a fact-finding mission to update information on the macro-economic situation," the official told Reuters.
The mission was due to arrive as politicians were trying to find a compromise on an election law that would allow new elections to take place at the end of June.

The elections are seen as vital to stop Albania, the poorest state in Europe, slipping back into the violence and rioting that erupted in February and March after the collapse of pyramid investment schemes.
Under previous projects, the IMF has lent around $60 million to Albania. The first project was a one-year standby credit in 1992 while a three-year structural adjustment credit was agreed in 1993.
However, that agreement ended after only two years as the Albanians and the IMF could not agree new terms to carry it on into the third year.

Although the current mission is only fact-finding, some Albanian politicians hope the country can negotiate fresh credits from the IMF once a new, stable government has been formed after the end-June elections.
